data.summary: Send an engine-supported channel message, continue after non-blocking output, or park and resume an interaction.

requiredFields.note: The bubbles this node sends, in order. Required and non-empty. One interactive bubble per node, and at most one blocking bubble.
One bubble. Its type picks a closed shape: the contract rejects any key that type does not declare.
One of the 18 types the engine parses. A PDF is 'file', a contact card 'contacts', quick replies 'quick_reply'. Not every channel renders every type.
On location, the required { latitude, longitude }.
On contacts, the cards to send. Every card needs all six keys (org, name, urls, emails, phones, addresses): send an empty object or array, never omit one.

optionalFields.note: Body text, in the channel's native formatting. Required and non-blank on text. WhatsApp caps: text 4096, buttons and flow body 1024. (when: Required and non-empty for text. A non-empty carousel body is required only by the WhatsApp branch.)
Optional id of the message. No effect on execution.
Optional flag, true once the message text was edited. No effect on execution.
On text, optional: 'html' marks the text as HTML. Its runtime use is not traced in workflow-core.
On text, optional: 'html' or 'rich', the authoring mode of an HTML text. No effect on execution.
Interaction settings. Only buttons, list, quick_reply, numbered_list, carousel, flow, webview and contact_info_request carry them; text carries only disableLinkPreview; other types reject settings.
Text messages only. true sends links without a WhatsApp preview card; absent or false keeps the preview. Honored by the WhatsApp Cloud API and Gupshup CAPI providers.
Optional boolean, on buttons, list and carousel. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional redirect object. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Memory key for a flow bubble's response; absent means 'response'. Only the flow type reads it: every other type stores under responseVariable.
Absent means false. true on a bubble without options makes exit and expire legal; a blocking contact_info_request waits for the contact. One blocking bubble per node.
Blocking contact_info_request only. true resumes on a shared contact that carries no phone; compared strictly, so the string 'true' does not count.
Re-prompt when a reply matches no option; the node keeps waiting. Absent: the bot's noValidOptionMessage, then a built-in text. On a blocking contact_info_request it answers any non-contact.
Read by the engine only on numbered_list; absent means true.
A boolean, not a text: there is no custom close text. true marks the sent buttons or list expired when the wait runs out. It does not route: an expire edge, when wired, does.
Optional redirect object for the expired case, the same shape as redirectPayload. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Webview: how long the run waits for the callback before expire. Absent or 0 falls back to the platform's cache limit.
Optional string. No runtime default reads it. Its runtime use is not traced in workflow-core.
Memory key for the selected option, or a webview callback's data. When set, the engine rewrites buttons, list and quick_reply options in place. Never written for contact_info_request.
Webview: text sent to the user while the run waits for the callback.
Optional: what pressing an already used button does. 'text' answers with redirectPayload.text, 'skill' redirects. Its runtime use is not traced in workflow-core.
Legacy one-time-use mode, a string, superseded by oneTimeUseType. Its runtime use is not traced in workflow-core.
Caption under the media or the body. Carried by buttons, image, video, numbered_list, flow, cta_url and webview; a sticker caption is accepted and dropped. Flow footer: WhatsApp caps it at 60.
Header text. Carried by buttons, list, numbered_list, flow, cta_url and webview. Needed on flow; WhatsApp caps the buttons and flow header at 60.
Rich header for buttons and cta_url: { type: 'text', text } or { type: image | video | file, url }.
'text' for a text header, which takes no url; 'image', 'video' or 'file' for a media header, which requires url.
Header text.
Media URL of an image, video or file header. Required there: an absolute URL, or a {{template}} that resolves to one.

The choices. Required on numbered_list. WhatsApp: buttons at most 3, list at most 10 rows. (when: Required as an array for numbered_list. Optional for url_buttons because that parser branch defaults absence to an empty array.)
One choice. buttons, quick_reply, list and numbered_list options take id, title and payload; url_buttons options take title, url, id, type and order.
List row subtitle. WhatsApp warns above 72 characters.
Stable option id; its edge is option:<id>. Non-blank, no colon, unique in the node. Never derive it from an array index.
Image URL for the option. Its runtime use is not traced in workflow-core.
Numeric position. Routing never uses it: route by id.
A string, on buttons and list. How it expands is not traced in workflow-core.
Routing payload carried with the pick, an object that keeps extra keys: targetId names the node the pick routes to, type the payload kind.
The label the user sees. WhatsApp caps a button at 20 and a list row at 24.
Option kind, e.g. 'postback'.
URL the option opens: the url_buttons type uses it.
Optional display order of the option, an integer. No effect on routing: route by id.
Optional subtitle of the option. Its runtime use is not traced in workflow-core.
Media URL for image, video, file, sticker and audio. Required there: an absolute URL, or a {{template}} that resolves to one. (when: Required for image, video, file, sticker and audio.)
On file, the document's display name. On location, the pin's name.
On location, the pin's address text. Optional.
On list, the label of the button that opens it. Absent or empty means 'Menú'. WhatsApp caps it at 20.
Required on flow, cta_url and webview. flow: { flow_id, flow_cta, flow_action, flow_action_payload, ... }; cta_url and webview: { display_text, url }. (when: Required for flow, cta_url and webview.)
On flow, an optional payload object. Its runtime use is not traced in workflow-core.
On carousel, 'image' or 'video'. WhatsApp requires it.
On carousel, required. WhatsApp wants 2 to 10 cards, a mediaUrl on each, and the same button count on all of them. (when: Required for carousel.)
Data-loss-prevention settings, passed through to dispatch. workflow-core does not execute them.
The name the author gives the node, e.g. 'Preguntar datos al usuario'. Every node type accepts it. A label only. No effect on execution.
Per-node non-happy-path handlers. Absent: the workspace handlers apply. Present, even empty: they replace the workspace handlers for this node.
Handler the engine runs when this node fails with no edge to follow. The only entry it looks up on non-conditional nodes.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler the engine looks up when a CONDITIONAL node fails with no edge to follow.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler for the exit event. Accepted; the engine does not look it up on a node today.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler for the expire event. Accepted; the engine does not look it up on a node today.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler for the invalid_input event. Accepted; the engine does not look it up on a node today.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Completeness flag stored with the node, false on a new node. Its meaning differs between node types. No effect on execution.
Tracking events emitted after the node runs, at most 10. Each fires when enabled is true and emitOn matches the outcome.
One tracking event: its name, when it fires, an on/off switch and the payload fields.
Event name, recorded as the track name. Up to 255 characters.
false keeps the event configured but never emits it.
When the event fires: 'always' (default when absent), 'success' on a successful run, 'error' on a failed one.
Fields added to the event, each resolved from memory and context when it fires.
One payload field of a tracking event.
Row id of the payload field. No effect on execution.
Key of the value in the event payload. An entry with an empty field is skipped.
Template resolved when the event fires, e.g. '{{$memory.orderId}}'. $env and $secret are not available; a resolution error stores ''.
Optional event id. No effect on whether the event fires.
Optional event kind; 'track' is the only value. No effect on execution.
Optional provenance, 'user' or 'ai'. Copied into the track record when present.
Optional creation timestamp. No effect on execution.
Optional last-update timestamp. No effect on execution.
Copy of the node's collapsed display state. No effect on execution.
Copy of the node's free-text comments. No effect on execution.
Copy of the id of a workflow the node was stored in. The node belongs to the workflow that stores it. No effect on execution.

branchTokenRules.when: never in an authored file: the engine has an alert outlet, but on every CHANNEL_MESSAGE shape `jelou workflow validate` rejects an 'alert' edge or drops it, so it never fires

branchCases.when: any message carries messages[].options[] (buttons, list, quick_reply, numbered_list, ...), and no webview
branchCases.note: Wire one 'option:<id>' edge per option id. Validate does not require it, but an option with no edge dead-ends the flow when picked. 'exit' and 'expire' are optional: wired, the engine follows them when a blocking bubble's wait ends; absent, it sends its own exit / expired text and ends the turn. No 'default'.

branchCases.when: a 'contact_info_request' message with settings.isBlockingEnabled=true, and no options
a 'buttons' / 'list' / 'carousel' message with settings.isBlockingEnabled=true, and no options
any other message with settings.isBlockingEnabled=true, no options, no webview
no webview, no options, no settings.isBlockingEnabled=true

unauthorableOutlets.reason: Contract pins the constant handle 'dynamic-button'. The CLI reaches dynamic buttons through the option:<id> grammar, which carries the configured option id instead of the constant.

outletDocs.description: The ordinary continuation: the node sent its bubbles and moves on. On a blocking contact_info_request it is the contact reply, the only route to the number.
outletDocs.fires: Right after sending when no bubble blocks: every default edge fires, in stored order; none wired completes the node. On a blocking contact_info_request, when a contact arrives.

branches.description: The next step after the message, or the shared contact on a blocking contact_info_request.
branches.when: Only on a node with no options and no webview; never 'success'. Required on a blocking contact_info_request. Elsewhere optional: a last message can end with no edge.

outletDocs.description: The node sent an interactive bubble and is parked, waiting. Not an edge: the run resumes through an option, exit, expire or error.
outletDocs.fires: When a blocking or interactive bubble is sent. The run stays parked and nothing is routed.

outletDocs.description: The user picked a configured option. Each option routes on its own edge, matched by the option id.
outletDocs.fires: When the reply names this node and a configured option id. Every edge wired to that id fires, in order.

branches.description: One edge per option, carrying that option's id after 'option:'.
branches.when: One per option id. Beside them a node with options takes exit and expire, both optional, and no default edge.

outletDocs.description: A reply for this node that matches no configured option, taken by the engine's dynamic-button fallback. Not authorable in a workflow file.
outletDocs.fires: When no static option matches the reply and a dynamic-button edge exists.

outletDocs.description: The interaction ended without a pick. On a webview it is the successful callback, not a cancel.
outletDocs.fires: On a blocking bubble, when the user exits (a cancel expression or the exit number). On a webview, when its callback reports success. None wired completes the node; a bubble sends its exit text first.

branches.description: Skip path of a blocking bubble, or a webview's successful callback.
branches.when: Required on a blocking buttons, list or carousel bubble with no options; optional on a node with options; a webview exit. Rejected on a non-blocking node without options and on a contact request.

outletDocs.description: Nobody answered before the wait ran out.
outletDocs.fires: When a blocking bubble's wait times out; a webview waits settings.expirationTime, else the platform's cache limit. None wired completes the node; a bubble sends its expired text first.

branches.description: Timeout path. Route it to a real timeout branch, never back to the same node.
branches.when: Required on a blocking bubble with no options and on a blocking contact_info_request; optional on a node with options; one of a webview's three exits. Rejected on a non-blocking node without options.

outletDocs.description: A reminder before expiry, while the node stays parked. Not authorable in a workflow file: no CHANNEL_MESSAGE shape takes an alert branch.
outletDocs.fires: When the expiration alert fires. The interaction remains parked.

outletDocs.description: The webview page's callback reported a failure.
outletDocs.fires: When a webview callback arrives with a failed outcome. None wired completes the node.

branches.when: Only on a node with a webview bubble, as one of its three exits with exit and expire; illegal on every other shape.

notes: contact_info_request is WhatsApp's request-phone button (Studio calls it 'Solicitar contacto'). Set settings.isBlockingEnabled true to wait for the number, and wire 'default' for the shared contact and 'expire' for the timeout — the engine has no cancel path, so it re-sends settings.optionNotFoundMessage until a contact arrives and 'exit' never fires. The reply is NOT stored in memory: the next node reads $message.contacts[0] ({ name, phones: [{ phone, wa_id, type }], addresses, emails }), so persist it immediately with a MEMORY node ({{$message.contacts[0].phones[0].wa_id}} — wa_id is digits only, phone is the display form) or CODE. The engine resumes on a contacts message only when it can read a phone off the card (wa_id, else phone, digits only); a contact shared without one re-sends settings.optionNotFoundMessage and the node stays parked, with no branch out. settings.allowContactWithoutPhone true (compared strictly) accepts any contact instead, and then {{$message.contacts[0].phones[0].wa_id}} stores an empty string rather than failing (the engine formats with skipUndefined), so guard on a non-empty value before trusting it. A forwarded third-party vCard does resume it, so verify the number belongs to the sender before trusting it.

Keep blocking contact_info_request default/expire legs disjoint unless the join is idempotent. Production evidence shows expire can dispatch milliseconds after a valid contact resumes default; `jelou graph reconvergence` and the validator's concurrent_branch_reconvergence warning identify the first shared descendant.

CHANNEL AVAILABILITY — read the workflow's channel off its filename infix (workflows/<slug>.<channel>.json, also in `jelou status` as `channel`) and pick a subtype the channel can render. WHATSAPP: every subtype EXCEPT quick_reply (WhatsApp's equivalent is 'buttons'). WEB: text, buttons, image, video, audio, file, location. FACEBOOK: text, buttons, quick_reply, image, video, file, carousel, webview, url_buttons. INSTAGRAM: text, buttons, quick_reply, image, carousel, webview, url_buttons. TWITTER: text, numbered_list, image, video. The `channel` validation phase reports the rest — 'flow' is a hard error off WhatsApp and blocks push; the others warn. Matrix source: Studio's per-channel message palette, re-read 2026-09-04 — re-sync it against Studio whenever a channel gains a block.

Provider-gated on WhatsApp: 'flow' and 'contact_info_request' need provider whatsapp_cloud|gupshup_capi|aldeamo, 'cta_url' and 'webview' need gupshup|whatsapp_cloud|gupshup_capi|aldeamo, and 'carousel' needs whatsapp_cloud. Webview shares the CTA list because the engine emits it as a CTA_URL bubble. The channel type alone does not tell you — `jelou channels show <channelId>` prints `provider`; `jelou workflow validate --provider <slug>` checks an offline file, while `jelou push` resolves the linked project's active channels automatically.

Channels with no documented palette rules: OMNICHANNEL and ELEVENLABS. CUSTOM, TEAMS, SLACK and EMAIL have explicit Studio palettes and are validated like the other known channels. Do NOT fall back to WhatsApp's allowlist for an unknown channel.

One interactive bubble per node, and at most one blocking bubble — two of either in the same node is a quality error. A blocking contact_info_request counts as that bubble and cannot share a node with an option-bearing one: its 'default' + 'expire' contract and the option edges cannot both hold.
Reply routing matches both the target node ID carried by the event and the selected option ID.
Use dynamic-button only when no static option matches for the same reply target.
Static reply option IDs must be stable and unique within the authored interaction; never derive them from array indexes.
Request and alert paths remain parked; exit, expiration, and error paths complete when no matching connection exists.
Non-blocking messages continue through every default edge in stored order; absent default edges complete the node.
A blocking interactive message selects its routed candidates but stopExecution prevents immediate execution while the input remains pending.
Outbound CHANNEL_MESSAGE accepts only the 18 message types handled by the Brain V5 message parser; INPUT keeps its separate request vocabulary.
Precondition: The selected channel supports every authored message subtype and interactive capability.
Precondition: A WhatsApp carousel requires non-empty body text; other channel branches do not establish that global requirement.

messages.text: What would you like to do?

settings.optionNotFoundMessage: I didn't understand. Choose one of the options.

rules: Never write a START node. The tool adds the workflow's one START (`validate --fix` and `jelou push` write it), unless the workflow enters only through a WEBHOOK.
Your first edge is { "sourceId": "START", "targetId": "<first-node>", "branch": "default" }. "START" is a reserved alias the tool resolves to the real START id; no other node may use that id.
The first node cannot be START, WEBHOOK, EMPTY, NOTE.
WEBHOOK is optional, at most one per workflow, and never chained to START.

A workflow or tool that enters only through a WEBHOOK needs no START: write no edge from "START" and the tool adds none. A channel message or a TOOL node never starts it then. A marketplace skill always needs START.
Next to a wired WEBHOOK that feeds the flow, a START with no edge is only a warning: the tool wires nothing to it and push keeps it.
